title: Model supply arbitrage & regional adoption signal hub
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: build a repeatable signal hub that surfaces model supply arbitrage (latency/cost/availability delta across regions and vendors) and regional adoption signals tied to product use cases. The hub should inform: routing policies, Dedicated capacity procurement, and sales GTM priorities.

Scope:
- Define a compact signal set (availability, license/terms change, quantization compatibility, latency tiers by region, hardware affinity, price trend) and the minimal ingest pipeline to collect these signals weekly.
- Build a weekly ranked feed (CSV + dashboard + Slack alerts) that flags high-risk or high-opportunity model changes by region.
- Deliver a small automation prototype (crawler + heuristics) and a lightweight human review process for false positives.

Success metrics (first 90 days):
- Signal recall: manual audit finds >= 80% of major model availability changes in target markets (US/EU/APAC) within 7 days.
- Signal precision: <= 20% false positive rate after human review.
- Business adoption: 2 internal teams (Routing & Dedicated sales) onboard the feed with at least one decision informed by it.

Deliverables:
- Signal taxonomy doc (Confluence) and mapping to actions.
- Ingest pipeline (market-intel repo) and weekly runner.
- Dashboard (Console/Sheets) + Slack alerting for P1 events.
- Onboarding doc for Routing, Sales, and Solutions teams.

Data sources & heuristics:
- Public model catalogs (Hugging Face, Model Zoo mirrors), vendor status pages, open-source release tags.
- Price and availability signals via lightweight probes (endpoint latency pings to hosted variants) and GPU spot/region price scrapes where allowed.
- Licensing signals by scanning model READMEs and vendor license pages for key term changes (commercial/enterprise-only, source-availability).

Constraints & trade-offs:
- Breadth vs depth: prioritize a 30-model whitelist representing top customer-facing variants rather than chasing entire ecosystem initially.
- Automation fragility: accept higher false positives in exchange for coverage; human review will act as gate for alerts to Routing.
- Data privacy/compliance: do not probe private vendor endpoints or customer-only endpoints; rely on public docs and vendor-provided status pages.

Stakeholders:
- Product (Aisha P., Diego M.), Routing lead (Priya Rao), Dedicated sales (Evan Kim), Research infra (SRE contact TBD), Solutions Eng (Lina Cho).

Acceptance criteria:
- Signal taxonomy and mapping reviewed and approved by Routing + Sales.
- Ingest pipeline integrated into market-intel repo and scheduled weekly runner in staging.
- Dashboard shows historical signal timeline and team can subscribe to Slack alerts for P1 events.

Next steps (this ticket):
1) Finalize 30-model seed list and region coverage (Aisha) — due 2026-02-26.
2) Prototype a rule-based crawler (Diego) to pull availability and license pages — POC by 2026-03-05.
3) Build Confluence taxonomy page and share with Routing/Sales — review meeting 2026-03-09.
4) Wire Slack alert for critical license or availability flips (SRE + Diego) — staging by 2026-03-20.

Notes: prioritized markets = US, EU (FR/DE), APAC (SG/JP). Initial model whitelist focuses on open models with >1k stars or known enterprise variants (quantized and full-fp). Will expand to closed-source vendor variants after establishing signal hygiene.
